```{r}
# function to define the B3 lab theme
theme_B3 <- function () { 
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major  = element_blank(),  # remove major gridlines
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),  # remove minor gridlines
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"), # center & bold
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold") # center & bold 
    )
}
```

#Get general data together:
```{r}
data_pw_t <- read.csv("/Users/AprilBooth/Desktop/Dissertation/Chapter2_cropmilk/R_markdowns/parent_weight_d4.csv")
```
```{r}
data_pc_m <- read.csv("/Users/AprilBooth/Desktop/Dissertation/Chapter2_cropmilk/R_markdowns/parent_cropmilkquality.csv")
```

#then need to join the two data sets together
```{r}
data_p_combo <- right_join(data_pw_t, data_pc_m, by="sample")
```
#now can find percent crop weight to body weight
```{r}
data_p_combo$percent_w <- ((data_p_combo$crop_sac_mass_g/data_p_combo$weight_d4)*100)
```

#change parental_state descriptions
```{r}
data_p_combo <- select(data_p_combo, -"treatment")
key <- read.csv("/Users/AprilBooth/Desktop/Dissertation/keys/parent_key.csv")
data_p_combo <- left_join(data_p_combo, key, by = c("sample", "nestid"))
#rename treatment groups
data_p_combo$treatment[data_p_combo$treatment == "single female"] <- "single mother"
data_p_combo$treatment[data_p_combo$treatment == "single male"] <- "single father"
data_p_combo$treatment[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired female"] <- "paired mother"
data_p_combo$treatment[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired male"] <- "paired father"
#get sex category
data_p_combo$sex[data_p_combo$treatment == "single mother"] <- "female"
data_p_combo$sex[data_p_combo$treatment == "single father"] <- "male"
data_p_combo$sex[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired mother"] <- "female"
data_p_combo$sex[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired father"] <- "male"
#get nest type category
data_p_combo$type[data_p_combo$treatment == "single mother"] <- "single parent"
data_p_combo$type[data_p_combo$treatment == "single father"] <- "single parent"
data_p_combo$type[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired mother"] <- "paired parent"
data_p_combo$type[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired father"] <- "paired parent"
```
# counting actual samples measured
```{r}
data_p_combo %>% count(treatment)
```

### Crop weight/body
##Graphing data to see how it looks:
```{r}
crop_weight <- ggplot(aes(y = percent_w, x = treatment, fill= treatment), data = data_p_combo) + geom_boxplot() + scale_fill_manual(values = colors_parent) +
  labs(title = "parent crop weight to body weight ratio", x="", y="% crop weight/body weight") + geom_point(pch = 21, position = position_jitterdodge()) + theme_B3() + scale_x_discrete(limits=c("paired mother","paired father", "single mother", "single father")) + theme(text=element_text(family="", size=16)) +theme(axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black",family="", size = 16)) + theme(legend.position = "none") + ggsignif::geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("paired father", "single mother")), map_signif_level = TRUE, y_position = c(7), test= "wilcox.test", textsize = 9) + ggsignif::geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("paired father", "single father")), map_signif_level = TRUE, y_position = c(5.5), test = "wilcox.test", textsize = 9) + ylim(0,8)
crop_weight
```

#now do ANOVA analysis
```{r}
leveneTest(percent_w ~ treatment, data = data_p_combo, center = mean)
```
```{r}
leveneTest(percent_w ~ brood, data = data_p_combo, center = mean)
```
# so need to rank transform
```{r}
lmer_w <- lmer(rank(percent_w) ~ treatment+brood+(1 | nestid), data = data_p_combo, REML = TRUE)
Anova(lmer_w, type = "II", test = "F")
```
# So there appears to be a significant difference between the crop weights by treatment groups. 
```{r eta}
eta_squared(Anova(lmer_w, type = "II", test = "F"))
```
###Post-hoc analysis difference between percent crop weights
```{r}
emmeans::emmeans(lmer_w, list(pairwise ~ treatment), adjust="tukey") 
```
#use emmeans, have significant difference Paired males vs Single Females, and Single Males.

## Cohen's d effect size test
#subsets of treatment groups
```{r}
pmom <- data_p_combo[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired mother",]
pfath <- data_p_combo[data_p_combo$treatment == "paired father",]
smom <- data_p_combo[data_p_combo$treatment == "single mother",]
sfath <- data_p_combo[data_p_combo$treatment == "single father",]
```

# paired fathers v single mothers
```{r}
pfath_v_smom <- full_join(pfath, smom)
cohens_d(percent_w ~ treatment, data = pfath_v_smom)
```

#paired fathers v single fathers
```{r}
pfath_v_sfath <- full_join(pfath, sfath)
cohens_d(percent_w ~ treatment, data = pfath_v_sfath)
```

#nest type and sex
```{r}
leveneTest(percent_w ~ type, data = data_p_combo, center = mean)
```
```{r}
leveneTest(percent_w ~ sex, data = data_p_combo, center = mean)
```
# so need to rank transform
```{r}
fit_pw <- aov(rank(percent_w) ~ type*sex, data = data_p_combo)
Anova(fit_pw, type = "II")
```
# So there appears to be a significant difference between the crop weights by nest type and sex.

```{r}
eta_squared(Anova(fit_pw, type = "II"))
```

#omitting NA data for analyzing crop milk quality scores
```{r}
data_score <- data_p_combo
data_score <- na.omit(data_score)
```
# count sample size for scored crop milk
```{r}
data_score %>% count(treatment)
```

### Crop milk color
```{r}
crop_color <- ggplot(aes(data_score$color, fill=treatment), data = data_score) + stat_count(width = 0.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors_parent) + labs(title = "Parent Crop Milk Color", x="Crop Milk Color", y="Count") + theme_B3() + theme(text=element_text(family="", size=14)) +theme(axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black",family="", size = 12)) + theme(legend.position = "right")
crop_color
```
#ordinal categorical data, so do fisher exact test
#make sure color numeric, factor for some reason
```{r}
data_score$color <- as.numeric(as.character(data_score$color))
```

```{r}
tbl_color <- table(data_score$treatment, data_score$color)
tbl_color
```

```{r}
fisher.test(tbl_color, simulate.p.value = FALSE, hybrid = TRUE)
```
```{r}
cramers_v(tbl_color)
```

# so no significant differences in color.

###Crop milk consistency

```{r}
crop_consistency <- ggplot(aes(data_score$consistency, fill=treatment), data = data_score) + stat_count(width = 0.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = colors_parent) + labs(title = "Parent Crop Milk Consistency", x="Crop Milk Consistency", y="Count") + theme_B3() + theme(text=element_text(family="", size=14)) +theme(axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "black",family="", size = 12)) + theme(legend.position = "right")
crop_consistency
```
#ordinal categorical data, so do fisher exact test
#make sure consistency is numeric
```{r}
tbl_consistency <- table(data_score$treatment, data_score$consistency)
tbl_consistency
```

```{r}
fisher.test(tbl_consistency, simulate.p.value = FALSE, hybrid = TRUE)
```
# effect size
```{r}
cramers_v(tbl_consistency)
```

# so no significant differences in crop milk consistency
